items.summary: The creator of Prince of Persia on why every generation has its defining prince.

content.v: When I started working at PC Gamer in 2014, I began what I didn't realize at the time would become a bit of a ritual. A few weeks before the San Francisco Game Developer's Conference that year, I sent the creator of one of PC gaming's first masterpieces, Prince of Persia, an email asking if he'd be in town. Jordan Mechner politely responded that he wouldn't be making the trip from his home in Paris to San Francisco that year. But I kept trying when the conference rolled back around, thinking maybe this would be the year the stars aligned.

It took a decade, but in 2024 we finally made it happen: Mechner joined a roundtable I hosted alongside other veterans from designing PC games in the '80s and '90s to explore their long careers. Afterward, we talked some more just one-on-one—but in the busy aftermath of the conference, that interview never ended up making its way online.

So here it is now, covering his autobiographical graphic novel, why we may not have seen the last of adventure game The Last Express , and how every generation of fans now has its "own" Prince of Persia.
The many princes of Persia

When this interview was conducted, Ubisoft hadn't yet canceled its remake of Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time , which would've been the first new 3D game in the series in 15 years. The latest 2D game, The Lost Crown , was still fresh, and would be followed not long after our conversation by another 2D game, The Rogue Prince of Persia.
PC Gamer: It's interesting to see different visions of the Prince existing simultaneously now, though obviously Prince of Persia has evolved many times over its history.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pn27oLmYkoP3cbsj8nkg5V-1920-80.jpg

Jordan Mechner: I think the Montpellier team made really smart choices with The Lost Crown, and doing Prince of Persia as a 2D Metroidvania, with an emphasis on the fantastic elements and the visual style that harks back to anime. It's also reminiscent of the early 2D Prince of Persia games and of the first Sands of Time.

Even fans of the 2008 Prince of Persia , I think, will find in the mythology and a lot of visual elements things that will make this feel like a Prince of Persia game to them in the best way. With no risk of it being confused with a photorealistic, fully 3D AAA Sands of Time-type game.

I loved the 2008 Prince of Persia. That game got a bad rap: People were like 'it plays itself. You don't have to do anything.' But I thought the fluidity of the movement in that game was just incredible. I loved it.
It's incredible to be part of something that's had so many lives.
Jordan Mechner

And the visuals are absolutely beautiful. There's, there's a lot to like about the 2008 Prince of Persia, and from my vantage point, from what I hear from fans, it has its own devoted, passionate following. Just as much as the Sands of Time trilogy, or the original 2D game.

That's the funny thing about Prince of Persia: That these constituencies are so separate, that there's all three of those. And then there's the Prince of Persia movie, because for many people, especially people who are around 30 years old today, the Prince of Persia movie is Prince of Persia for them, because they weren't the right age to have played any of the games.
There's a new generation of gamers for whom The Lost Crown will be the first Prince of Persia they encounter. It's incredible to be part of something that's had so many lives.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/oRYTFQXaKqj5UigbsUeXon-1920-80.png
It's slightly surreal for me to hear you say the word 'Metroidvania' because it's such a gamer genre, but it also didn't exist when you made the original.

Of course, I made Prince of Persia about the same time that Metroid and Castlevania were being made. So it's a term that didn't exist, and we didn't have genres in those days in the sense that we do now. I think all of these we would have called platform games or action adventure games.

I don't know if you played Castlevania: Symphony of the Night, or some other version of a Metroidvania? What did it feel like for you having made a platformer that set a lot of precedents, and seeing that genre evolving over the years?

I've never been a Metroidvania player—I would say Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown is actually the first Metroidvania game that I've played and really gotten into as a player. And I'm just enjoying it so much. As a 2d gamer, games that stand out to me are Inside and Limbo, which I thought were really beautiful. I also enjoyed some of the recent Rayman games.
Do you remember much about Prince of Persia 3D? Did you work on that game or consult on that game at all?
That was an internal Broderbund project. So I wasn't on the team, but I knew them.

I had been at Broderbund when I was making Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame, which was my last, Broderbund Prince of Persia game. After that I had the idea to do a third episode of the trilogy in 2D. But this was 1993, tthe year of Doom and online multiplayer shooters, and so doing a 2D game just kind of didn't excite publishers, the way it had a year earlier.

So instead of that, I created Smoking Car Productions and The Last Express. While we were making The Last Express, Broderbund, then I think partly looking at Tomb Raider, came around to the idea of doing Prince of Persia as a 3D game. I wasn't involved, but wished them well. And they kept me in the loop.
Do you remember playing that one?
I played the first two levels. It was on PC, and I was a Mac gamer. So it wasn't really my genre, I didn't have a PC that was powerful enough to really enjoy it. So I only saw a bit of it.

Today I hear surprisingly often from gamers that they really enjoyed Prince of Persia 3D and have fond memories of it. So we should probably add that to the list of versions of Prince of Persia that each have their little camp.

I've never played it, but I'm really curious now to go back. It sounds like there wasn't anything you took directly from it. But I'm curious what was going on in that time between Prince of Persia 3D coming out, and you making your own 3D version with Sands of Time?

When I saw Tomb Raider I I was impressed. It blew my mind: it was the first third-person real-time 3D game I'd seen. I was making The Last Express at the time, which was a very different kind of game. But seeing Tomb Raider, I thought 'well we don't need to do Prince of Persia in 3D now. They've just done it. And it's great.'

But seeing Tomb Raider, and then seeing Prince of Persia 3D a few years later, my feeling as a gamer was that I missed the speed and fluidity of 2d gaming. Advancing up to the edge of a block and trying to point yourself in the right direction, and then missing the jump, as a gamer I just had more fun playing the 2D games. Of course, this was a stage in the evolution of 3D. So when I met the Ubisoft Montreal team in 2002, and they pitched the idea of doing a Prince of Persia for the PlayStation 2 generation, my first reservation was, 'how well is this going to work in 3D?'
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/sJYpJnirCXb3YPMSiwPD89-1920-80.jpg
The decision, from Sands of Time to Warrior Within—the mandate to change it from Teen to M was a marketing mandate. It wasn't the team's idea.

items.title: 质量效应粉丝在时代广场购买#SaveMassEffect 广告牌 - 他们还计划购买更多
items.summary: Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week,

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/26/save-mass-effect-billboard-times-square-2-1793032285351.png
Mass Effect fans have bought a #SaveMassEffect billboard in Times Square after EA shut down BioWare last week, but the fight to save the sci-fi RPG franchise isn't stopping there.

Whether New York City residents are familiar with Commander Shepard's fight against the Reapers or not, everyone in Times Square was alerted to #SaveMassEffect when its billboard went up today. It's the latest in a string of moves from the community backing the sci-fi RPG franchise and its developers as they work to give them a second wind.

"Keelah si'yah," text on the billboard said. It's a reference to the in-universe language of Khelish, which is spoken by the Quarian species. According to the Mass Effect Wiki , the line specifically translates to "by the homeworld I hope to find one day."

🚨 WE'RE IN TIMES SQUARE! Together with @kalaelizabeth, we've managed to get a #SaveMassEffect billboard up in Times Square, NYC, all day today! 📍 1560 Broadway, above the Pelé store (Duffy Square) ⏰ 15 seconds every hour at :35 HOLD THE LINE! ❤️ https://t.co/wNP9Ak9Vh8

Those supporting #SaveMassEffect come from all over, but the billboard featured in Times Square on this late-October day came from a smaller group known as We Are Mass Effect, a community dedicated to paying tribute to the franchise started in summer 2025 by a 27-year-old in Spain named Ariel Peña Aguilar . He, along with his second-in-command and partner María 'Mer' Mora , as well as X/Twitter user Kala Elizabeth , sought to publish the billboard in hopes of drawing attention to their cause.

The idea originally came from Aguilar and Mer before Elizabeth was brought in for assistance and is part of their goal to keep Mass Effect alive. So far, their efforts include emailing EA directly, contacting Canadian politicians , and doing everything they can to draw more attention to their cause. The best part? Their Times Square billboard is just the beginning.

Aguilar told IGN that community organization around canceled Star Wars project The Hunt for Ben Solo is partly what inspired his push to save Mass Effect. He added, "I thought something like that could work really well for our situation, too."

Our beloved @drowwpoison, co-ceo of We Are Mass Effect, who's been working incredibly hard to give the #SaveMassEffect movement even more power, went to see our billboard in Times Square, New York City! ❤️ ✍️ Sign the petition: https://t.co/AhcEFDBbd0 https://t.co/69jfSoxyci

"At first, I thought it might be a bit of a crazy idea," Aguilar said of the billboard, "but then I brought it up with my project partner, Mer, and the incredible content creator Kala Elizabeth, without whom none of this would have been possible. We all agreed it was worth doing, and we started organizing everything. And we have more plans! The billboard is just the first step."

There's a natural question that comes up whenever there's a grassroots push like this: How much does it cost to put up a billboard in Times Square? Well, at least on a Monday in October, it's only about $250. Both Aguilar and Elizabeth confirmed the financial cost of boosting #SaveMassEffect wasn't the issue. Instead, it was copyright hangups that gave them more trouble than anything, even if it's now a "fun anecdote," according to Aguilar.

"We initially had someone else make a different graphic, but it said 'BioWare' in it, so we had to change it last minute because of copyright," Elizabeth told us. "There was a lot of back-and-forth in a rush to fix it, and I had to remake it myself. I did end up using the wrong Mass Effect saying because I've been thinking about the author Catherynne Valente, who announced she had been working on Mass Effect 5 , and she had written a previous novel about the Quarian ark for Andromeda. Keelah si'yah is that ark. It's still somewhat fitting of the intent, but we mean keelah se'lai. Oops."
Lots of great feedback in the comments. Our next billboard will be simpler and include a QR code to the petition!

As if there was ever any doubt, there are millions of people who still care about Mass Effect. Aguilar clarified that We Are Mass Effect isn't directly affiliated with the major petition going around, even if they do "fully support the petition and the effort behind it." For him, they are "simply fans trying to use every tool and resource at our disposal to support the cause and make sure this movement continues for as long as possible."
Aguilar sees the joint effort as "a message of unity" in the aftermath of decisions made by EA "that goes far beyond our concern for Mass Effect or Dragon Age." This is about more than video games.

"At the end of the day," Aguilar added, "these franchises are works of art, and while they mean an enormous amount to us, we're also deeply concerned about all the developers who have lost their jobs, as well as those who may still face layoffs in the future, especially during such a difficult period for the video game industry."

He continued: "They're the ones who deserve our support the most. We're going to hold the line." It should be said, though, that no one here is under the illusion that EA has any intention of changing course – or even listening.

As Mass Effect fans work together for another trip among the stars, dissenting opinions have seen naysayers push back against any hope at a revival. Aguilar mentioned the billboard team is "familiar with EA's track record when it comes to how they treat their IPs and developers," adding, "it's easy to understand why fans would feel defeated from the outset." Even if expecting change from EA is a "naïve and unrealistic expectation," they'll continue to push forward anyway.

"Unfortunately, I think we all know that EA probably does not care," Elizabeth added, "but amidst all the horrible press right now around EA's new owners, Jared Kushner and the Saudi government , I hope their track record of killing games becomes another topic of the conversation. This is, albeit, just a small part of the corrupt government and sports washing conversation around EA's new owners, but is absolutely part of it.
The #SaveMassEffect petition just hit 200,000! Absolutely insane work by everyone, keep it up! ♥️ https://t.co/tHiNeNhmCt

"SaveMassEffect is also about trying to save media. History. BioWare was a pillar of Edmonton for 30 years, and EA bought them out and shut them down like they have done for now 20 studios. I don't want them to sit on IPs and let them die. Mass Effect, Dragon Age, and Dead Space are just a few, and they all deserve better. What happens when this massive debt they've accrued closes EA, too? Then what?

"This is about the preservation of media and preserving the work of the studios that EA keeps killing. We don't even know if EA let BioWare try to buy themselves out or let someone else buy them before they closed the studio, canceled the game, and fired the 50 employees keeping BioWare together. What they're doing is wrong. BioWare deserved better. The employees deserved better, and the fans deserve better, too.

items.title: 微软计划裁员 25% 以上
items.summary: An employee buyout offer is reportedly being extended to roughly 60,000 Microsoft employees in the US, UK, Ind

content.v: Microsoft has announced a new "voluntary exit offer" aimed at making drastic cuts to its headcount. A CNN report says roughly 60,000 of the company's employees are eligible for the buyout offer, a number that represents around 27% of its total workforce.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support. It also gives participating organizations another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," Microsoft chief people officer Amy Coleman said in a memo sent to employees .

"The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter. This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program."

The CNN report says Microsoft's buyout offer is part of its effort to balance its spending on AI services, and was preceded by its first-ever voluntary buyout program for employees in the US in April, and then layoffs of roughly 4,800 people in July.

The buyout offer is limited to employees in the US, UK, India, and Canada, and not all employees are eligible: Coleman said participation in the program "varies based on each business's priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs." Employees who want to take advantage of the buyout will leave the company on December 31, according to the CNN report.
Whether Xbox is one of the participating businesses was not specified—I've reached out to Xbox to ask and will update if I receive a reply.

items.title: 新的 Windows 11 Insider Experimental 版本增加了无需浏览器即可检查互联网速度的功能
items.summary: A small change, but a handy one.

content.v: If you are part of the Windows 11 Insider program, you may have finally received the option to test your internet speed directly from Quick Settings in the latest experimental build. That means no more going to a browser to see if your new broadband package is as speedy as advertised.

Those using Insider Experimental build 26340.9767 can simply click on Quick Settings and scroll down to see a speed test button (via Windows Latest ). You can also find the network icon in the system tray, right-click it, and then select "Test internet speed". This will give you your download and upload speeds.

Up until now, Windows 11 users have been able to access an internet speed test from Windows settings, but clicking on it redirects you to a browser and then runs the test via Bing. It's a small barrier but still an annoying hurdle to get to a fairly simple tool.

Alongside this, Preview Build 26340.9767 adds feature flags (so you can filter your machine by which options are enabled / disabled), Quick Settings now gives access to mobile phones, it adds a Magnifier keyboard shortcut, it gives an easier way to access your Microsoft 365 subscription, and a few other things.

If you'd like to get access to the latest Insider Preview Builds, you can simply register to become an insider , then go into your Windows update settings, and select the latest option. Naturally, there's some risk with trying out developing tech, and the experience likely won't be as smooth as the traditional Windows build, but you do get access to some new features early.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/yEMK6QNhtXcquwrZJYVkoB-1920-80.jpg

As well as this, there's technically no guarantee that any Insider updates will actually come to the stable build of Windows 11. Insiders are sort of like beta testers for Windows software, and if enough feedback suggests the implementation is poor, Microsoft could listen to that and remove it from future updates.

Still, being able to check your internet connection speed without accessing a browser feels like an uncontroversial update. Skipping any barriers to get that information quicker feels beneficial to the end user, and I can certainly see myself using it next time I need to test it. Or, most likely, if I want to complain about how slow my speed is going on a given day.

items.title: 《羊蹄之魂》开发商 Sucker Punch 遭遇裁员
items.summary: Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of

others.title: 《Ghost of Yotei Dev Sucker Punch》遭遇裁员，领导层着眼于下一个 PlayStation 项目

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2025/09/25/scwk6j-1758769803399.jpg
Ghost of Yotei developer Sucker Punch has laid off some staff, just a little over a year after the release of its last game.

Aftermath reported that the studio let 26 employees go, just weeks after Ghost of Yotei's DLC and Complete Edition were released on PS5. The studio has roughly 200 employees as it stands. Aftermath shared an email that was sent out to the team from studio leadership, which reveals that "challenges in the market" and changes in the scope of the team for its next project were the deciding factors in the layoffs.

“After carefully observing the challenges in the market and reviewing the team needs for our next project, we've decided to make some staffing reductions. Several positions across Sucker Punch will be eliminated as a result," the email reads.
The note also stated that they will discuss the plans for the studio's future next week.

”We know this is a lot to take in, and we want to assure you that we did not make this decision lightly. We have given this a lot of attention and worked to support our affected colleagues during this transition as well as we can. … There's no getting around that this is a hard day. Next week we will go into more details about the future.”

As of right now, it's unclear what Sucker Punch's next game will be; it does sound like there is another project in the cards based on the studio's statement. Some want a return to Infamous, whether through a collection of remasters/remakes or a brand-new entry. Others want a new Sly Cooper. And of course, there's appetite for more games in the studio's Ghost series. It wouldn't be surprising if at least one of these happens, as new IP with a big AAA budget is becoming harder and harder to justify.

Ghost of Yotei was one of the biggest games of fall 2025, selling 3.3 million copies in its first month . It's also one of the best-reviewed PS5 exclusives to date. It was also expected to come to PC at some point, but unfortunately, that plan was scrapped when Sony opted to move away from PC . The game recently got a Complete Edition , which added a brand-new story DLC and other additional content. It's unclear if this moved any significant copies or if the audience for the game already capped out with its initial release.

The layoffs also come during a tumultuous time for PlayStation, which has been upsetting fans over its controversial shift to an all-digital future starting in 2028 . The company will phase out physical copies of games in favor of digital releases, likely beginning with PS6. PlayStation also shuttered Bluepoint , a beloved studio that was best known for high-quality remasters, ports, and remakes such as Demon's Souls for PS5. Additionally, PlayStation attempted to scrap development on Hideo Kojima's next gen game, Physint, until Microsoft swooped in to save it .

items.title: 现在，一整套 Steam PC 游戏都可以在越狱的 PlayStation 5 上本地运行，包括《传送门》、《Left 4 Dead 2》等等
items.summary: I never thought I'd see the day.

content.v: What a time to be alive. Gamers are starting to play Steam games locally on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles, thanks to several projects that aim to bring PC gaming to the Sony-loving masses. One such project is Playden for PS5 , which was made publicly available earlier this month.

The program functions as a Steam launcher, but also creates a private Windows environment via prospero-win, a port of Wine for PlayStation 5 (via Videocardz ). The software has support for up to Direct3D 11 through DXVK and Direct3D 12 games through VKD3D-Proton, and includes a separate runtime kit for the graphics drivers, along with specific app shells for the games themselves.

"It downloads a game, prepares it, and hands it to a separate PS5 app made for that game. That app starts Wine with the game's settings," says the readme on the project's GitHub page. "Because each game is its own app, it has its own tile on the PS5 Home screen, and it is isolated: its files, settings and crashes stay inside it."

Reddit user Cevap has posted a video of their jailbroken PS5 playing Portal locally . "Game runs as you expect," says Cevap. "Only issue being you can’t use a mouse cursor, nor can you press ESC to go to the options. Otherwise basic controls work. What an amazing project, thank you!"

In the case of Playden for PS5, the GitHub page stresses that the software is in an early alpha state, so it's probably best not to expect too much from it at this stage. The compatible games list is pretty chonky, though, including some pretty big hitters. Just be prepared for crashes if you give it a go yourself.

It must also be mentioned that, aside from the risks of jailbreaking a PS5 in the first place, users also need to log in to their official Steam accounts to use the software. "Valve does not support third-party clients," say the devs "We know of no account problems from this, but the risk is yours to accept."

It's also quite an involved process to get it working by the looks of things, so this is probably one for advanced users. Still, I guess I can chalk this up as "things I thought I'd never see." An increasingly long list in 2026, it seems.

items.summary: Money where your Meowth is. We've heard all kinds of wild Pokémon resale stories over the years, but this one

content.v: Money where your Meowth is.

We've heard all kinds of wild Pokémon resale stories over the years, but this one might just be the craziest of the bunch and has left us ringing our parents telling them to get up in the loft and look for our old collections again.

items.title: Valve 表示将研究此事后不到十分钟就向 Steam Frame 内核添加了 CD-ROM 支持

content.v: You can truly never anticipate how one might use their tech. After a Steam Frame owner asked why the VR headset didn't work with their detachable disc drive , Valve developer gaberow said they were looking into it—and patched in kernel support mere minutes later.
As spotted by Tom's Hardware , AiodensGhost asked for the feature on October 18, gaberowe responded on October 19, then made the commit to the Steam Frame kernel in less than ten minutes.

If you're wondering why someone would want CD-ROM support, AiodensGhost says, "I wanted to use my Steam Frame to be able to watch a movie on the road, and thought it was no big deal to use the detachable disc drive I had on my computer."

They continue, "Turns out that the Frame cannot power the player and even if it could it lacks the drivers to read a disc. Valve, this not only killed my ability to watch a movie, IT KILLED MY ABILITY TO INSTALL MY ABANDONWARE FROM 2006. You don't sell NFS Carbon anymore."

The mention of Need for Speed Carbon is interesting here, as it suggests one might opt to boot up a game on the Steam Frame from a CD-ROM drive, rather than streaming one from a library. Carbon is not officially on Steam (or any legal digital storefronts as far as I can see), so the only way to legally play some games on the Steam Frame would be via an old disc.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vY4ztJVBw6dNr9Zr4sVMMT-1920-80.jpg

The Steam Frame does seem primarily built for use in VR games, but given its comfort and screen, it would make sense why one might enjoy it for 2D games and movies. CD-ROM support would make the device a little more versatile.

One thing that is worth noting here is that kernel-level support doesn't mean that all Steam Frame units will officially gain the feature. It means Valve could implement the change in a future Steam Frame update should it want to. Given the public reply from a developer and the kernel change, my money is on official support arriving in the future, but Valve could always opt not to do so.

Should you want to add it yourself, you can install the kernel on your device via the ' Deckard Linux no oopsies ' repo, instead of waiting for any sort of official update. But I'd hazard a guess that those looking for disc drive support are fairly few in the first place.

We learnt that Sue Storm and Doctor Doom will be joining the fray as playable characters in the last news drop, and today, we've finally got some details on the expansion's new game mode.
